krs.text: **Understand each change and next decision.** In real human games, the User can follow casting, targeting, resolution, combat, damage, death, and turn changes and identify whose decision is next. **Express every intended legal play without awkward controls.** Maintain an explicit interaction-family and known-friction ledger for the selected matchup, including large and rare choice sets and the full Learn/Lesson interaction. Every reported awkward action blocks closure until reproduced, fixed and confirmed. Preserve complete legal choices and server Command authority; record exercised and untested coverage. **Finish and choose to return.** The User completes games against clearly identified trained checkpoints and voluntarily chooses to play again. Retain all attempted sessions, including abandonment, with match, world, opponent, deck/seat and reproducible Command identities; discover and remove additional stopping friction through those sessions. Agree the concrete human-play cohort before scoring it, revisit repaired interactions across later sessions, and exercise both deck assignments. Automated terminal fixtures do not substitute for this human outcome.

## Original scope (historical)

Prepare the next repository chapter through start-chapter, proposal-only until the present human accepts the reconciled plan. This Task is the archival/planning worktree, not permission to implement product features or mutate the existing portfolio.

Human accepted direction on 2026-09-24: exactly one Project per continuing Wave and three KRs per Project; proposed roster Game, Intelligence, Rules with Study folded into Game. Train bots that can beat the User in the currently demoed GW Allies versus UR Lessons matchup. Getting the User to play full games is equally central. Missing transitions and overwhelming action choices are concrete friction; even one awkward intended action makes them stop. Discover further friction through actual play rather than asking the User to diagnose it in advance. Carry forward existing dispositions as evidence: ETU-21 abandoned; ETU-31 experiment deferred; ETU-55 provider-only ship distinct from calibration closure; preserve ETU-34/PR179 work. No new decks beyond content/pool support needed for the existing matchup.

The human is present in the controlling conversation. Return open questions and the final proposal there; do not use lf ask or create another human session. items.name: Make bench_branching source_sha256 reproducible across checkouts
items.description:
W2-198 merged at 09ac3405 with both receipts verifying IN ITS WORKTREE, but NEITHER verifies on merged main. Both fail 'source digest mismatch'. This blocks KR2's 'one REPRODUCIBLE harness' clause: the receipts are unverifiable by anyone except the (now-deleted) worktree that produced them.

MEASURED, not inferred (2026-07-16, at merge commit 09ac3405):

* git diff --stat 2f2781e origin/main => EMPTY. Identical git tree. Both checkouts clean (git status --porcelain => 0 lines).
* Yet source_sha256 differs:
    canonical main /Users/jack/src/manabot          => 549f6738cd5b610ac7a8ee63eea607c0075d8d2890599af360a432cf1739076f
    task worktree  ...implement-compact-clone-plus-undo => ba778d315bf1aab095c8eb5adeea7a0161184f1fc8d7a3c1820cc2c78e46c634
    receipts record ba778d31... (the worktree's), so verify fails on main.
* File counts entering the walk: main 197,361 vs worktree 510.

TWO ROOT CAUSES in scripts/bench_branching.py source_sha256():

1. '.claude' is not in excluded_parts. The canonical checkout nests agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-*/**, so ~197k unrelated files (other branches' full source trees) are hashed as 'source'. Any agent activity anywhere changes the digest.
2. '.git' is excluded only as a DIRECTORY name. excluded_parts filters os.walk's dirnames. In a LINKED git worktree, .git is a regular FILE containing 'gitdir: /abs/path', so it survives into filenames and is hashed -- making the digest depend on the worktree's absolute filesystem path. (Diff of the walk sets shows exactly: only-in-TASK = ['.git']; only-in-MAIN = ['.claude/...'] x197k.)

CONSEQUENCE: source_sha256 binds a receipt to the incidental contents and path of the directory that generated it, not to the source it claims to measure. verify() can never pass on main, in CI, or in a fresh clone. This is the same class of failure that left W2-182's receipt red on main and is why that repair did not stick.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (implementer decides): bind the receipt to the SOURCE, not the working directory. Options: (a) hash the git tree/commit of the tracked, contract-relevant paths (managym/src, managym/tests, scripts/bench_branching.py, docs/benchmarks/search-branching-contract-v1.md, Cargo.lock) via git rather than an os.walk of the filesystem; or (b) keep the walk but restrict it to an explicit allowlist of contract-relevant paths and exclude .claude plus any .git entry whether file or directory. (a) is strictly more reproducible and makes the receipt verifiable from any clone at that commit; it also removes the whole-tree brittleness where an unrelated wave/ doc edit invalidates every receipt.

ACCEPTANCE: at the landing commit, 'uv run scripts/bench_branching.py verify' and 'verify --driver compact_clone_undo/current_game_v1' both pass FROM THE CANONICAL MAIN CHECKOUT (not only from the generating worktree), and re-running them from a second independent checkout of the same commit yields the identical digests. Regenerate both receipts under the corrected scheme. Do NOT change measured workload semantics, fixtures, seeds, or the contract ID; this is a provenance fix, not a re-measurement of the candidates. Keep the serial gate: no page-COW, no representation selected (W2-199 owns those).

items.name: Materialize possible-world batches without re-enumerating support
items.description:
## Chapter disposition — approved 2026-09-24

REWRITE REMAINING SCOPE. The prepared possible-world provider is shipped in main (e856a90); preserve provider parity, identity, batching and complexity receipts. Scientific calibration remains DEFERRED and is not completed by that provider merge. The prior record-learnings Run run_400f18cda0a34be0843e9c74ab552291 explicitly retained calibration as open and requires a pre-generation preregistration check. Reconcile the old ship/lifecycle record before any lifecycle closure; do not rerun or resume calibration from an automatic recommendation. Revisit only for a demonstrated challenger-training need with a separately frozen protocol and authorization.

## Original scope (historical)

INT-17's frozen v1 calibration run exposed an authoritative provider complexity bug. FrozenPolicyLikelihood loops each row in one PossibleWorldSpace and calls root_space.materialize(row); Env.materialize_possible_world currently rebuilds PossibleWorldSpace::for_viewer and recursively enumerates the entire support for every row, making one likelihood update O(S^2). At the frozen 121,485-row maximum this is about 14.76B row-enumeration operations per update, and the run stopped after 1h38m with only commitments through ordinal 2. Build the narrow Rules-owned, identity-checked prepared materializer that enumerates one canonical space exactly once per immutable likelihood root and materializes many canonical indices without re-enumeration. The prepared provider object must survive across every inference batch for that root: the proof target is exactly one PossibleWorldSpace::for_viewer construction per likelihood update, not one per row or one per batch. Stream bounded materialized batches and release their isolated Env branches before the next batch; do not retain all S branches simultaneously. Preserve exact ordering, physical-deal weights, viewer-safe identity, source revision and viewer-state validation, deterministic seeded isolated branches, materialization mode semantics, and fail-closed stale or mismatched identity behavior. Migrate FrozenPolicyLikelihood to the production prepared/batch surface and make wall, CPU, and RSS caps observable/checkable between inference batches rather than only after a whole decision ordinal. Prove single-index and batch parity against the existing provider, add debug Rust and uv-managed Python regression coverage including the exact construction call-count plus scaling/peak-RSS evidence, and retain measured complexity and throughput receipts. Do not edit or rerun the immutable INT-17 v1 contract or its failure receipt: the repaired provider necessarily changes engine/source/extension fingerprints. Instead publish the repaired provider receipt and complete runtime identities, then preregister experiments/contracts/int-17-belief-calibration-v2.json. The v2 validator must canonically copy v1's trace, likelihood checkpoint, algorithm, cohort, preflight, metrics, prediction, caps, arena interpretation, and exclusions exactly; refresh only provider_receipt and expected_runtime; preserve identity stream 8d9f46fa86742f323f915ba69bc0007e225415e8fc5504792eac4b49ebae66b6 with zero provider gaps; and fail before generation on any scientific drift. Rerun v2 within the existing 6h and 2GiB caps. Do not change the cohort, thresholds, belief semantics, or move possible-world authority into manabot.
